# Execution Feedback and Action Correction

Manipulation Action Models → Multi-Fingered Dexterous Hand Manipulation Research → Tactile Manipulation → Execution Feedback and Action Correction

Dexterous manipulation whose main contribution is using measured tactile feedback or proprioceptively inferred contact to intervene in execution, refine actions or trigger retries. State the sensing source, feedback-to-command interface and whether weights change. Distinguish inferred contact from calibrated force and execution supervisors from learned action policies. Review papers individually rather than automatically migrating tactile-tagged records.

| [AM.MAN.DEX.VLA.FEEDBACK.1] <a id="am-man-dex-vla-feedback-1"></a> | **AgenticTactileVLA｜Agent execution supervision · Fixed VLA · Proprioceptive contact feedback**<br>[AgenticTactileVLA: Contact-Guided Execution-Time Supervision for Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation without VLA Retraining](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.04391v1)<br>Elizaveta Semenyakina, Ivan Snegirev, Mikhail Kiselev, Miguel Altamirano Cabrera, Artem Lykov, Hajira Amjad, Dzmitry Tsetserukou<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` [vla](../../../topics/vla.md) `execution-feedback` `action-correction` `proprioception` [contact-estimation](../../../topics/tactile.md) `compliant-control` `grasping` `pick-and-place` `real-world` `agentic-execution-supervision` `fixed-vla` | AgenticTactileVLA wraps a fixed VLA with an execution-supervision Agent that infers contact from finger-motion mismatch and motor effort, pauses subsequent motion and corrects individual finger closure when grasp support is insufficient, then retains the correction or returns control to the VLA for retry, without extra tactile sensors or VLA retraining.<br>**Evaluation scope:** The base GR00T-N1.6-3B is fixed after teleoperation fine-tuning. It reads images, instructions, robot state and measured hand positions, and outputs body-motion tokens and six-channel hand-position targets. An external, nonlearned stateful supervisor detects insufficient support at terminal closure from commanded-versus-measured finger motion; motor-effort deviations additionally guide per-finger adjustment. Only body-reference progression pauses, while stabilization remains active. Passing the support criterion retains the corrected configuration; otherwise the hand override is released so subsequent VLA commands can reopen and re-approach. Releasing the override does not itself command reopening. Weights remain unchanged; corrected measured hand positions enter subsequent observations. Before closure, language cues or a VLM can select a predefined current-limited compliant mode; the VLM does not generate controller parameters. Proprioceptive feedback is contact evidence rather than calibrated force, with no extra tactile hardware. Unitree G1 with BrainCo Revo2 is evaluated on five held-out objects, 15 matched trials per object, with a shared 60-second/three-approach budget. Completion rises from 61.3% to 84.0% (72.0% for unconditional close-to-stall). The compliant branch evaluates object integrity during closure and holding, not autonomous transport; cross-hand and cross-VLA generality are not established. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.04391v1) | Initial reading<br>2026-11-04 |
